title: Alternative-Fuel Vehicles Hit Record 40% of India's Car Sales as Iran War Drives Fuel Switch
excerpt: Electric, hybrid, and CNG vehicles claimed an unprecedented share of passenger vehicle sales in June as surging petrol prices push Indian consumers toward cheaper alternatives.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Alternative-fuel vehicles reached 40.35% of passenger vehicle sales in June, up from 38% in May.
  • Overall vehicle sales surged 21.8% to 2.6 million units, with passenger vehicle sales rising 28.6% year-on-year.
  • Electric two-wheeler penetration crossed 10% for the first time; Tata Motors led electric car sales with 12,187 units.
  • Fuel price hikes from the Iran war prompted consumers to switch to cheaper vehicle alternatives.
  • Industry analysts warn that geopolitical uncertainties may impact future demand.

  • Alternative-fuel vehicles reached a record 40.35% of passenger vehicle retail sales in June, up from 38% in May
  • Overall vehicle sales surged 21.8% to a record 2.6 million units, with passenger vehicle sales rising 28.6% year-on-year to 410,853 units
  • Electric two-wheeler penetration crossed 10% for the first time; Tata Motors led electric car sales with 12,187 units and 38.3% market share
  • Fuel price hikes triggered by the Iran war drove the shift, though FADA president warns it may be a "knee-jerk reaction" rather than a sustained trend

A Tipping Point for Indian Mobility

India's automobile market crossed a milestone in June 2026: alternative-fuel vehicles accounted for more than 40% of all passenger car sales for the first time. The shift, driven by soaring petrol and diesel prices after the Iran war triggered multiple fuel price hikes in May, marks the fastest adoption of non-fossil-fuel vehicles the country has seen.

According to the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA), CNG models led the alternative-fuel category with 24.3% of total passenger vehicle sales, followed by hybrids at 8.3% and electric vehicles at 7.8%. Overall passenger vehicle sales rose 28.6% year-on-year to 410,853 units.

> **"Tata Motors retained its leadership with 12,187 units and a 38.3% market share, posting 126.7% year-on-year growth."**

EV Sales Shatter Records

Electric passenger vehicle sales reached 31,823 units in June, a 107.8% jump from the previous year and a 19.3% increase over May. Tata Motors retained its leadership with 12,187 units and a 38.3% market share, posting 126.7% year-on-year growth. Mahindra secured second place with 7,766 units, growing 121% year-on-year.

JSW MG ranked third with 5,861 units, followed by Maruti Suzuki with 1,919 units in its first full year of EV sales following the eVitara launch. Vietnamese manufacturer VinFast continued expanding with 1,404 units, while BYD grew 51.3% to 873 units.

In the two-wheeler segment, electric penetration crossed the double-digit mark for the first time, reaching 10.6% of total sales. Total EV registrations across all categories hit 305,678 units in June, according to the government's Vahan Dashboard.

The Iran War Effect

The catalyst for the record shift was unmistakable: fuel price hikes. After petrol and diesel prices were raised several times in May following the Iran war, consumers rushed to vehicles with lower running costs.

Maruti Suzuki, India's largest carmaker, reported that bookings for its CNG vehicles jumped 40% since the fuel price hikes. The broader automobile industry posted record numbers, with total retail vehicle sales across all categories climbing 21.8% to about 2.6 million units.

What Comes Next

Industry analysts attributed the strong June performance to favourable financing conditions, tax relief measures, resilient rural demand, and a wider range of alternative-fuel models. But experts cautioned that geopolitical uncertainties, supply-chain challenges, and fluctuations in fuel prices could influence demand in the second half of the year.

FADA noted that while the worst of the crude shock and supply chain disruptions from the Iran war appeared to be over, a return to complete normalcy could still take "a few quarters" and may involve cost implications. For NRI investors tracking Indian auto stocks, the data confirms a structural shift that is reshaping the competitive landscape, with Tata Motors and Mahindra emerging as clear EV leaders while traditional combustion-engine dominance erodes.
